native_result.query: Between which two races is the factor of BA degree completion -0.9568 when compared to the other?
native_result.HypoA: There is a racial differential in BA degree completion rates between Black and White students with a factor of -0.9568.
native_result.HypoB: Between which two races is the factor of BA degree completion -0.9568 when compared to the other? Answer: Black and White. In a logistic regression of BA DEGREE COMPLETED on race dummies, SES, and a race-by-SES interaction (NLS, n=8773, White reference), the Black-vs-White coefficient is -0.9568 (fitted -0.956778, OR 0.384): at equal SES, Black respondents have substantially lower log-odds of BA completion than White respondents.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Inspection: 8773 rows; races White 5337/Black 2113/Hispanic 1323; no missing or zero codes in ASVAB, PERCENTILE, SES, BA (BA is boolean; SES negatives are real standardized values). 2) Descriptives by race and raw BA rates (Black 1.33%, Hispanic 1.44%, White 3.54%); raw log-odds contrasts bracket the target (Black-White -1.006, Hispanic-White -0.924). 3) Specification search: 942 contrasts across 32 covariate-subset logits (unadjusted and standardized), all three reference codings, pairwise two-race logits, sex-stratified fits, LPM, probit, AME scales, and race-by-covariate interactions; compared each log-odds contrast (and odds-ratio/AME scales) to -0.9568 with tolerance +/-0.005. 4) Unique exact match: logit with race + SES + race*SES (uncentered SES), Black vs White = -0.956778 (dev 2.2e-05); no other specification within +/-0.005; closest non-match was race-only Hispanic vs White (-0.9241, dev +0.033).

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: There is a racial differential in BA degree completion rates between Black and White students with a factor of -0.9568.

sub_hypo.text: In the NLS sample of 8,773 respondents, a logistic regression of BA degree completion on race, SES, and race-by-SES interactions, with White as the reference, yields a Black-versus-White coefficient of -0.956778 (approximately -0.9568; odds ratio 0.384).
sub_hypo.context: NLS participants with social background and academic resources measured at secondary school graduation; full sample of 8,773 respondents. The model uses uncentered SES and White as the reference race.
sub_hypo.relations: Logistic regression with race dummies, SES, and race-by-SES interactions. The Black-versus-White main-effect coefficient is -0.956778, corresponding to an odds ratio of 0.384 at SES = 0. Because the model includes race-by-SES interactions, the Black-versus-White log-odds contrast at other equal SES values also depends on the interaction.
